Hi everyone,

I’m looking for an experienced automation developer who can help me build a video conferencing automation system using n8n + MirrorFly + API integrations.

This is a paid freelance project with clear requirements and a defined scope.

I’ll keep this as concise and technical as possible so you know exactly what’s involved.

Project Overview

I need to build an automated video conferencing workflow using n8n and MirrorFly that will:

  • Create video meetings automatically based on predefined triggers.

  • Generate meeting details and share them with participants.

  • Schedule meetings using calendar integrations.

  • Send meeting invitations and reminders through email or messaging services.

  • Manage meeting related events through webhooks and APIs.

  • (Optional add-on) Automate meeting recordings and post meeting notifications.

All of this needs to run through n8n workflows, with MirrorFly providing the video conferencing capabilities.

Core Requirements

1. MirrorFly Video Conferencing Integration

  • Integrate MirrorFly Video Call API and SDK.

  • Create and manage video meetings through supported APIs.

  • Generate or retrieve meeting joining details.

  • Handle meeting events through webhooks or callbacks where supported.

  • Support one to one and group video calls.

  • Connect MirrorFly with n8n using HTTP requests, webhooks, or a custom integration where required.

2. Meeting Scheduling and Management

  • Trigger meeting creation from form submissions, CRM updates, or other events.

  • Integrate with Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar scheduling services.

  • Send meeting invitations to participants.

  • Schedule automatic reminders before meetings.

  • Handle meeting cancellations and rescheduling.

3. Automated Notifications

  • Send meeting details through email or supported messaging services.

  • Notify participants when a meeting is scheduled, updated, or cancelled.

  • Send reminders at predefined intervals.

  • Support optional Slack or Microsoft Teams notifications.

  • Use structured data to pass meeting details between workflows.

4. CRM Integration

Integrate with HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive to:

  • Trigger meeting workflows based on CRM events.

  • Associate meetings with relevant contacts or deals.

  • Update CRM records when meetings are scheduled or completed.

  • Store meeting details and supported recording links.

5. Post Meeting Automation

  • Trigger workflows when a meeting ends, using supported events or callbacks.

  • Send follow up emails to participants.

  • Update CRM records with meeting status.

  • Store meeting metadata and recording links when available.

  • Trigger additional workflows based on meeting outcomes.

6. Optional Premium Feature: Meeting Recording and Streaming

If you have experience with video recording and streaming integrations, please mention it.

This feature may include:

  • Automating meeting recording through supported MirrorFly capabilities.

  • Retrieving recording details or links.

  • Triggering workflows when recordings become available.

  • Integrating supported RTMP or HLS streaming workflows where required.

Tech Stack

You must be comfortable with:

  • n8n: Webhooks, HTTP Request nodes, conditional logic, API integrations, and asynchronous workflows.

  • MirrorFly: Video Call API, SDK integration, and supported meeting capabilities.

  • Calendar APIs: Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar services.

  • CRM integrations: HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive.

  • Backend development: JavaScript or other technologies when a custom integration is required.

Deliverables

  • Fully configured n8n workflows.

  • MirrorFly integration with the required video conferencing functionality.

  • Automated meeting scheduling and notification workflows.

  • Documentation for future maintenance.

  • One handover and training session.

  • 30 days of bug support after delivery.

Budget

The budget is flexible depending on experience, but roughly:

  • Base system: £800–£1,000

  • Advanced features and integrations: £800–£1,200

Payment can be arranged through an agreed platform.

How to Apply

Please reply with:

  • Your experience with n8n and API integrations.

  • Your experience integrating video conferencing APIs or SDKs, preferably MirrorFly.

  • Examples of similar automation projects.

  • Your availability.

  • Estimated delivery timeline.

  • Your pricing for the base system.

  • Your pricing for advanced features and integrations.

I’m ready to start immediately with the right developer.

Thanks!

  4. About 20 hours a week, US Eastern time (Detroit).

  5. I’d rather scope it after reading the MirrorFly docs than guess a number now. I’d give you a milestone breakdown with dates once the API surface is clear.

  6. I’d quote a fixed price for the base system after that scoping step. I won’t give you a number I can’t stand behind.

  7. Advanced features, such as the recording and streaming add-on, would get their own fixed quote after scoping. I haven’t built recording or RTMP/HLS workflows, so I’d verify what MirrorFly supports first.

I can walk you through the HubSpot and missed-call builds on a live screen-share, and you can reply here or DM.

Good day @Shyamvijay your project bridges asynchronous webhook event with deterministic scheduling, which introduces three specific architectural risk that most developers hit until they hit production.

First, relying on long static wait nodes for meeting reminder will inevitably fail when an event is rescheduled. The correct pattern is to maintain a single master database record for each meeting room tracking UTC start time, active time zone and current status. A scheduled n8n worker then polls this record on a rolling 15 minutes window to trigger reminder dynamically. This eliminates stale notification entirely.

Second risk is syncing both Google Calendar and a CRM. This creates bidirectional write conflict. One system should be designated as the strict source of truth, typically the calendar of event scheduling and the CRM for deal tracking. Any writes to the secondary system must be tagged with a metadata flag so n8n can filter them out during webhook processing. Without this tag, infinite sync loops that breaks the workflow logic will be generated.

Third risk, handling post meeting recordings requires careful compliance framing before any API calls reach your CRM. UK and EU recording regulations mandate explicit consent notices and defined retention windows. Your n8n workflow should capture the recording link, verify that consent flag is active and only then route the media metadata to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. This protects you from automatic compliance violation while keeping the data pipeline fully automated.

Good day @Shyamvijay your project bridges asynchronous webhook event with deterministic scheduling, which introduces three specific architectural risk that most developers hit until they hit production.

First, relying on long static wait nodes for meeting reminder will inevitably fail when an event is rescheduled. The correct pattern is to maintain a single master database record for each meeting room tracking UTC start time, active time zone and current status. A scheduled n8n worker then polls this record on a rolling 15 minutes window to trigger reminder dynamically. This eliminates stale notification entirely.

Second risk is syncing both Google Calendar and a CRM. This creates bidirectional write conflict. One system should be designated as the strict source of truth, typically the calendar of event scheduling and the CRM for deal tracking. Any writes to the secondary system must be tagged with a metadata flag so n8n can filter them out during webhook processing. Without this tag, infinite sync loops that breaks the workflow logic will be generated.

Third risk, handling post meeting recordings requires careful compliance framing before any API calls reach your CRM. UK and EU recording regulations mandate explicit consent notices and defined retention windows. Your n8n workflow should capture the recording link, verify that consent flag is active and only then route the media metadata to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. This protects you from automatic compliance violation while keeping the data pipeline fully automated.

Good day  @Shyamvijay  your project bridges asynchronous webhook event with deterministic scheduling, which introduces three specific architectural risk that most developers hit until they hit production. 
 First, relying on long static wait nodes for meeting reminder will inevitably fail when an event is rescheduled. The correct pattern is to maintain a single master database record for each meeting room tracking UTC start time, active time zone and current status. A scheduled n8n worker then polls this record on a rolling 15 minutes window to trigger reminder dynamically.  This eliminates stale notification entirely. 
 Second risk is syncing both Google Calendar and a CRM. This creates bidirectional write conflict. One system should be designated as the strict source of truth, typically the calendar of event scheduling and the CRM for deal tracking. Any writes to the secondary system must be tagged with a metadata flag so n8n can filter them out during webhook processing. Without this tag, infinite sync loops that breaks the workflow logic will be generated. 
 Third risk, handling post meeting recordings requires careful compliance framing before any API calls reach your CRM. UK and EU recording regulations mandate explicit consent notices and defined retention windows. Your n8n workflow should capture the recording link, verify that consent flag is active and only then route the media metadata to Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive. This protects you from automatic compliance violation while keeping the data pipeline fully automated.

Hi Shyam, one thing that usually causes problems on these meeting setups is when a reschedule happens after reminders have already been queued. 
 Instead of using long Wait nodes, store one row per MirrorFly room with the status, start time in UTC, and the time zones of the people joining. Then run a short scheduled workflow that looks at that row and sends only the reminders that are actually due. A cancel or time change just updates the same row, so nothing old gets sent. 
 Also decide early whether the calendar or the CRM owns the meeting time, and mark every record the workflow writes. That stops an update from n8n creating a second meeting by mistake. 
 If you add recording later and any participants are in the UK or EU, include a short recording notice in the invite and set how long those links stay on the CRM record. 
 That covers the create, notify, change, and log steps without the usual silent failures.
